TITLE:  
FLASH FORWARD

LOGLINE:  
During a chaotic 2004 electronic-music festival weekend, two estranged friends reunite when a disposable camera develops photographs of a crime scheduled to happen the following night—only to discover the final image shows one of them taking the picture.

HOOK:  
The first flash reveals a crime scene that does not exist yet. The second flash catches the two friends inside it.

SORA PROMPT — 12 SECONDS:  
Create one open-ended, high-paced 12-second premium streaming-series sizzler, realistic 2004 electronic-music festival atmosphere, handheld 35mm energy, sodium-orange security lights, strobes, rain-slick pavement, crowded night fields, distant sound systems, no logos or readable brand names. Open on a disposable camera exploding with flash in the hands of MAYA, 24, and ELI, 25, estranged former best friends pressed together in a frantic festival crowd; the photographs whip past the lens in impossible rapid succession: an empty service tunnel, a dropped silver key, a security gate buckling, then a photograph of the same tunnel filled with flashing police lights even though it is currently empty. The kick drum accelerates with each flash; analog camera click, crowd roar, distant MC fragments, rattling metal, and a rising distorted synth pulse form the soundtrack. Maya stares at Eli and whispers, “That’s tomorrow.” Eli grabs the final photograph; its image develops visibly in his fingers, revealing Maya in the tunnel holding the camera while Eli lies motionless behind her, then the live camera whips toward Maya as she raises the disposable camera and its flash blinds the frame. Hard audio cut to a single camera click, followed by a deep sub-bass impact and the title NIGHT SHIFT 2004 emerging as stark white analog timestamp numerals for one instant before dissolving into black.

TITLE:
**REWIND**

LOGLINE:
Two estranged best friends reunite at an underground 2004 electronic-music festival and discover disposable camera photos that seem to predict a crime—forcing them to confront fractured trust, surveillance, and whether they're seeing the future or someone else's confession.

HOOK:
A flash of neon in the dark. Two friends lock eyes across a pulsing dance floor, then a photograph falls between them—something impossible frozen in 35mm. Time folds backward.

SORA PROMPT — 12 SECONDS:

*Strobe-cut opening: grainy DV-cam aesthetic, neon purple and blue washes. Close-up of two hands—one reaching for a disposable camera in darkness, the other pulling back. Hard electronic beat drops. SOUND: deep synth stab, vinyl crackle underneath.* 

*Fast montage: crowded festival interior, laser grid cutting through fog, sweat-slick faces, hands up. A photograph spins into frame—grayscale image of an unfamiliar warehouse, shadow moving across concrete.* 

*Two friends (faces obscured by shadow and strobes) back-to-back in the crowd, confused, mouths moving (no dialogue audible—only music swells). One holds the photo up to neon light.*

*Flash-cut to security camera static. Clock ticking. Ambient industrial hum building under the beat.*

*Final frame: polaroid lands on concrete. Words appear in white typography: "DID YOU SEE THIS?" Beat drops. Black cut. Title card hits hard with synthesizer sting.*

*Tone: hyperkinetic, claustrophobic, urgent. Pure dread buried under rhythm. 2004 digital-video texture. No resolution—only question.*
